newsitem.title: UK: East Europe firms in emerging debt, Peru ignored.
newsitem.headline: East Europe firms in emerging debt, Peru ignored.

text.p: East Europe dominated what little trading there was on Friday in an emerging market which is generally stronger but seeing most investors sit out the last few days of the year.
The market rose on Thursday with the help of firmer U.S. Treasuries.

There was some interest in Bulgaria which has been recovering from fall-out earlier in the month. Traders still remain very wary of the high-yield debt until there is more certainty that the International Monetary Fund will come to the economy's rescue.
However, Finance Minister Dimitar Kostov offered investors some reassurance when he pledged that the government would meet its $130 million interest bill for Brady bonds, due on January 28.

There is speculation that unless there is a radical improvement in the way the Bulgarian economy is managed and it starts bringing in some money, 1997 could see Bulgaria become the first Brady country to default.
Russia is also stronger and most of the news coming out of the country this week has been positive, including the settlement, in principle, of the last major commercial debts to the West.
On Thursday, the government announced the agreement with creditors on some $5 billion in uninsured trade debts.
Vneshekonombank dollar paper RUVNUSLNS=RR, which had slipped on selling earlier in the week, was bid 1/4 of a point higher at 77-3/8 cents in the dollar.
"There's a lot of cash to spare and one of the few things that feel comfortable at the moment is Russia," one European bank trader said.
Peru debt, as usual during the London day, was untouched but remains under pressure as the hostage crisis in Lima drags on.
There were a few of trades in Brazil C bonds BR8D14=RR but prices were unchanged from New York levels.
